title: How many little triangles are in each stacked triangle?
description: The little triangles in the stacked triangles are counted row by row, and the rows have one, three, five, seven and nine. Adding the rows gives one, four, nine, sixteen and twenty five.
teaching_notes: One idea: each new bottom row has two more triangles than the row above, and adding these odd rows from the top gives the square counts. Watch for students who count only the upward triangles.

source: Figure it Out Q4 (Try This), p.12
video_script.why: The child counts the little triangles in each stack by adding the rows one at a time, using the method of the solved example where each new part adds a fixed number.
video_script.substitution: Little triangles added in a new bottom row are counted in place of the matchsticks added by a new triangle.
video_script.anchor: a row of stacks of little triangles, from one to five rows, with the rows counted
video_script.payoff_line: The little triangles are the square numbers, one, four, nine, sixteen and twenty five

final_answer.value: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, the square numbers; the rows have 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 triangles
final_answer.spoken: one, four, nine, sixteen and twenty five, the square numbers

maths_rules: the rows of the stack have 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 little triangles, two more each row
check: row 5 has 2 x 5 - 1 = 9 little triangles
adding odd numbers from 1 gives the square numbers
video_script.design: The stacks stand in a row with the rows of the biggest stack lit one by one. The row counts are added and compared with the stacked squares.

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, add the rows one at a time. The first stack has one triangle, and one plus three is four.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Four plus five is nine, and nine plus seven is sixteen. Sixteen plus nine is twenty five.

<bookmark mark='mult'/>Four is two times two, and nine is three times three. Sixteen is four times four, and twenty five is five times five.
